title: Contract on the Line
briefing: Friday 17:40. Valtren's largest pharma client, Halvern Biologics (11% of revenue), has found a vaccine shipment that spent 50 minutes above 8C in transit and was delivered without the excursion being reported. Their head of quality writes: 'We are considering terminating the contract under clause 14.'
The CEO asks you to lead the response.

context.text: Your open relationship with the regulator means you can call Imogen Raske directly.
Coldline 2's alerting should have caught this. Find out why it didn't.

evidence.title: Data logger trace
evidence.body: Shipment peaked at 9.4C for 50 minutes during a 70-minute unplanned stop. The in-cab alert sounded; the driver acknowledged it; no escalation followed.

evidence.title: Excursion procedure
evidence.body: Any excursion must be reported to the client within 2 hours and the load quarantined pending the client's decision. The driver was not trained on the pharma procedure; he was an agency driver covering a shortage.

evidence.title: Clause 14
evidence.body: Halvern may terminate for 'a material breach of temperature control or reporting obligations' with 30 days' notice. Annual contract value 5.6m.

evidence.title: Regulatory duty
evidence.body: Distributors must notify the Authority of excursions affecting medicinal products that reached a patient-facing site.

options.label: Confirm where the affected vaccine is and support Halvern's recall decision, notify the Authority as required, and check every other pharma load this week for unreported alerts
options.feedback: Patient safety, legal duty and the extent of the problem first.

options.label: Call Halvern's commercial director to save the contract
options.feedback: Commercial talks before patient safety and regulatory duty is the wrong order.

options.label: Investigate fully before telling anyone else
options.feedback: The regulatory duty and patient safety don't wait for your investigation.

options.label: Agency drivers placed on pharma loads without pharma training, and alerts that end with the driver instead of escalating to a control centre
options.feedback: Two control design gaps, not one driver's mistake.

options.label: The driver ignored the alert
options.feedback: The system relied on one untrained person.

options.label: The unplanned stop
options.feedback: The trigger, not the cause of the failure to report.

questions.prompt: How do you approach Halvern on Monday?

options.label: Meet their head of quality in person: full facts, root cause, what's already fixed, and their right to audit the fix
options.feedback: Ownership and transparency are the only route to keeping a quality-driven client.

options.label: Offer a 10% discount to stay
options.feedback: Price doesn't fix a quality failure; it looks like buying silence.

options.label: Argue the breach wasn't 'material'
options.feedback: Legal argument loses the relationship either way.

schedules.description: Halvern Biologics serves notice under clause 14

questions.prompt: Which fix do you commit to?

options.label: Pharma-trained drivers only on pharma loads, alerts routed to a 24/7 control desk with a 15-minute escalation rule, and weekly audit of alerts against reports
options.feedback: Fixes both causes and adds a detective control.

options.label: Retrain the driver
options.feedback: Fixes one person, not the system.

options.label: Ban agency drivers entirely
options.feedback: Over-reaction that worsens the driver shortage; training and allocation solve it.

questions.prompt: What do you tell the board?

options.label: Same day: what happened, patient-safety status, regulator notified, client position, root cause and fix, and the revenue at risk (5.6m a year)
options.feedback: Boards must hear bad news fast and whole.

options.label: Wait until you know whether Halvern stays
options.feedback: The board needs to know before the outcome, not after.

options.label: Leave it to the CEO
options.feedback: You lead the response; the board will want to hear from you.

lesson: In a client crisis: patient safety and legal duties first, then root cause in the system, then ownership and transparency with the client and board.
